title: Cache FX rates in Redis to cut currency service load
executive_summary: This change introduces Redis caching of FX rates with a 15-minute TTL to reduce currency service load; it directly modifies the Currency Service and API Gateway but affects 10 downstream components including Payment, Refund, and Order services. You must run the five P0 tests—TC-1041, TC-1044, TC-1039, TC-1043, TC-1031—which cover rate staleness, feed outages, cache recovery, and conversion timing (REQ-1005, REQ-1004). The risk score is CRITICAL (76) because 10 similar defects have happened before in this code, three were critical, and 14 components depend on the change; four high-relevance requirements lack attached test evidence despite having recommended tests (REQ-1004, REQ-1005). One key decision (CMT-1003, EV-3003) requires that unsupported currencies be rejected before funds are reserved, and one reviewer raised a gap (CMT-1008) about incomplete ISO-4217 validation in related code that was reopened twice.

ecr_overview.title: Cache FX rates in Redis to cut currency service load
ecr_overview.description: Introduce a Redis cache in front of the FX rate feed, with a 15 minute TTL and rate-age propagation. Infrastructure change plus a small currency service change; conversion arithmetic is untouched.

change_classification.summary: A Redis cache layer with 15-minute TTL is added in front of the FX rate feed to reduce currency service load, with rate-age propagation. Stale rate delivery, cache misses, inconsistent multi-currency conversions, and rate update delays could break currency conversion accuracy and payment processing timeliness.

sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.body: This change introduces Redis caching of FX rates with a 15-minute TTL to reduce currency service load; it directly modifies the Currency Service and API Gateway but affects 10 downstream components including Payment, Refund, and Order services. You must run the five P0 tests—TC-1041, TC-1044, TC-1039, TC-1043, TC-1031—which cover rate staleness, feed outages, cache recovery, and conversion timing (REQ-1005, REQ-1004). The risk score is CRITICAL (76) because 10 similar defects have happened before in this code, three were critical, and 14 components depend on the change; four high-relevance requirements lack attached test evidence despite having recommended tests (REQ-1004, REQ-1005).
